title: Quinoa vs. Lentils: Protein, Fiber, and Carbs Compared

seo.title: Quinoa vs. Lentils: Protein, Fiber, and Carbs Compared
seo.meta_description: Per 100 g cooked, lentils provide about 9 g protein and 8 g fiber; quinoa about 4.4 g protein and 2.8 g fiber. Their carbohydrate totals are similar.
seo.search_intent: Compare cooked quinoa and lentils for protein, fiber, carbohydrates, and calories.

excerpt: Lentils clearly lead on protein and fiber: per 100 g cooked they provide roughly 9 g protein and 8 g fiber, compared with about 4.4 g and 2.8 g in quinoa. Calories and carbohydrate are much closer, so the two foods play different roles on a plate.
content_html:
Quinoa and lentils are both described as plant-protein foods, but the numbers are not close. Lentils are much denser in protein and fiber; quinoa behaves more like a whole-grain side dish.

Per 100 g cooked

Cooked quinoa provides roughly 120 calories, 4.4 g protein, 21 g carbohydrate, and 2.8 g fiber. Cooked lentils are around 116 calories, 9 g protein, 20 g carbohydrate, and nearly 8 g fiber.

With similar calories and carbs, lentils provide about twice the protein and almost three times the fiber.

What quinoa does better

Quinoa has a balanced essential-amino-acid profile and a rice-like texture that makes it convenient as a grain replacement. It is also naturally gluten-free.

Lentils work better as the main protein base

A 200 g cooked serving of lentils provides roughly 18 g protein; 200 g cooked quinoa provides about 9 g.

They can work together

Quinoa can supply the grain-like base while lentils add legumes, protein, and fiber.

If the goal is more protein and fiber, lentils win. If the goal is a versatile gluten-free pseudocereal, quinoa fills a different niche.

faq.question: Which has more protein?
faq.answer: Cooked lentils, about 9 g/100 g versus roughly 4.4 g/100 g for quinoa.

faq.question: Which has more fiber?
faq.answer: Lentils, close to 8 g/100 g versus about 2.8 g/100 g for quinoa.

faq.question: Which has more carbohydrate?
faq.answer: They are very similar by cooked weight, around 20–21 g per 100 g.
